basis: Estimates derived from public data; not Singha figures.

run.method: fixed-seed Monte Carlo over the triangular and uniform inputs; central values use the modes and midpoints; 90 per cent intervals are the 5th and 95th percentiles of the draws, i.e. ranges from the stated input bounds, not calibrated statistical intervals
run.price_basis: listing price per can = mean of four online multipack prices read 20 Oct 2026 (record 68d); the D01 reading is a promotional selling price (408 struck through). Sensitivity cases are in price_cases.

csd_market_2025_thb_m.source: Five press values for the carbonated soft-drink market, read as a mix of windows: 67,000 (Bangkokbiznews 13 Oct 2025, 2025, no source named); 68,000 (ThaiBev executive, labelled 2024); 70,000 (Marketeer 17 Apr 2026 compilation, NielsenIQ and brand forecasts, 2025); 70,772 (NielsenIQ, 12 months to November 2024, as printed by Thansettakij 14 Jan 2025; not used as the mode); 76,900 (KResearch, 2025 forecast, via Thansettakij 8 Sep 2025). Central = median = 70,000. The central is not a 2025 actual: it mixes 2024 and 2025 values and one forecast (record 67). The market basis (retail or manufacturer) is not stated

lemon_soda_share_csd.source: Positioning, 4 July 2022 (https://positioningmag.com/strategic-move/88360; saved in rework/raw/diligence_2026-10-20/T7/positioning_2022_07_04_csd_share.md): Singha Lemon Soda 2.4 per cent of total carbonated soft drinks, and 1,450 million baht, given two years after launch. The article's 1,450 divided by its 62,725 (2021) is 2.31 per cent. The central 2.35 is the midpoint of the printed and computed shares. The year of the measurement is unresolved: 2021 or 2022 (launch dated August 2020 in record 69, so two years after launch is about 2022). The article's market value is for 2021. The 12 per cent share in the same article does not reconcile (1,450 over 13,172 is 11.0 per cent) and is not used. The band 1.5 to 3.0 per cent is an assumption of change between the measurement and 2025

listing_price_thb_per_can.source: Online retailer listing prices read 20 Oct 2026 (record 68d, S): 13.54 (Makro PRO 24-can), 13.75 (7-Eleven ALL Online 24-can, promotional selling price), 13.75 (Lotus's 24-can), 14.17 (Lotus's six-can). Central = mean of these four = 13.80. Top of range = single-can online list price THB 17.00 (Lotus's, S01, read 20 Oct 2026). The mix of pack sizes sold is not sourced, so the central is an unweighted mean. Not a store shelf price (none read)

estimate_1_can_volume_and_revenue.identity_note: Top-down net revenue = retail value x (net per can / listing price). The price level cancels, so the top-down revenue does not depend on which price is chosen; the price choice moves cans and the per-can economics.
estimate_1_can_volume_and_revenue.check_2021_value_note: The 1,357 million figure has no year printed in the saved text (T6/09). It equals the press volume of 28 million litres at THB 16 a can to within 0.04 per cent, so it may be a derived value, not an independent sales figure.
estimate_1_can_volume_and_revenue.basis_note: Market value level (retail or manufacturer) is not stated by any source; retail basis assumed. A manufacturer-value basis would lower the top-down cans. Not modelled as a separate case (stated limit).

estimate_2_share_of_singha_corporation.caveat: Conditional shares: they hold only if Singha Corporation booked the can. The booking entity is not identified. Press figures; no source named. The article prints the year 2568 (2025) for both revenue and net profit in the same sentence. Net profit share uses contribution before aluminium, labour, overhead, depreciation and tax, so it is not like for like with net profit. The two derivations share the same can volume, so they are not independent of estimate 1.

estimate_3_variable_cost_and_price.zero_contribution_formula: (net revenue after VAT, margins and excise, less all non-aluminium variable cost) divided by (sheet mass times FX); no aluminium price used

superseded_model_value_thb_per_can.note: records 58 and 61 model; includes aluminium at the 19 October saved LME reading, which is not authorised. Superseded by the non-aluminium cost above and the aluminium slope

estimate_3_variable_cost_and_price.derivation_A: Component build from records 58 and 61 with the aluminium line removed (bottom-up).
estimate_3_variable_cost_and_price.derivation_B_status: NOT an independent cost derivation. Peer full-cost check: each peer's full cost per can implied by its gross margin on the same net price. Peer margins include fixed production cost and are on sales of goods. The check shows the room left for aluminium and fixed cost; it does not test the component build. Stated limit: no independent second cost source for the can's non-aluminium cost was found.

estimate_3_variable_cost_and_price.note: Variable cost only. Excludes labour, overhead, depreciation, freight, distributor and marketing costs. Not comparable with full-cost peer margins.

derivation_B_top_down_peer_implied.read: Different bases: A is variable margin on the can; B is a full-cost margin implied by the peers. B is a basis check, not a second estimate of the same quantity. The room at the peer median is the amount left for aluminium and fixed cost. It is not a threshold.

estimate_5_line_capacity.tbc_singha_customer_note: Thai Beverage Can's filing names Singha Beverage Co., Ltd. as one of five main domestic customers, with no product or plant named (P, BJC One Report 2025; record 69)
estimate_5_line_capacity.read: No pouch, sachet or dry-solids line is evidenced at any group company. Line time is small at the assumed speeds. The co-packer minimum run (500,000 to 1,500,000 per SKU and formula) binds before line time does.

estimate_6_cannibalisation.derivations: A: displaced cans times can contribution, as a share of top-down can volume. B: the same ratio on bottom-up can volume. A and B are the same ratio on two denominators, so they are NOT independent derivations. The independent check is the net-change calculation (cube contribution minus can contribution), which uses a separate cube cost and price. Stated limit: no independent source for the share of cube buyers who are existing can buyers was found.
estimate_6_cannibalisation.read: Gross at-risk figures are upper bounds because the can contribution excludes aluminium. The net change is the cube contribution minus the can contribution on each switched unit. The cube cost excludes binder and flavour, which are not priced, and the cube's planning price of THB 15 is an assumption. 1:1 switch is an assumption.

estimate_7_pilot_fixed_cost_fit.headline_basis: chain basis: planning price THB 15 through the same VAT, margin and excise chain, after excise, less THB 4.09

derivation_A_model_basis_ex_factory_9_00.status: Before excise, so not on the same basis as the chain figure. Shown for reconciliation with submission 05 only; not in judge-facing ranges.

estimate_7_pilot_fixed_cost_fit.read: Steady-state break-even ignores discounting and the year-0 cost, so it sits below the model's NPV break-even. Both bases use the same fixed cost. The headline is the chain basis, which is after excise. The cube price is a planning assumption. Pilot fit does not depend on the can volume.
